articles.title: Why Doki Doki Literature Club Bet on Ren'Py and Python: The Niche Engine Behind a Free Horror Phenomenon
articles.excerpt: Doki Doki Literature Club! should not have scared anyone. A free cute dating sim, made in a Python visual-novel engine most Unity developers have never opened, with static 2D sprites and no voice acti…
articles.body: Doki Doki Literature Club! should not have scared anyone. A free cute dating sim, made in a Python visual-novel engine most Unity developers have never opened, with static 2D sprites and no voice acting — yet it became one of the most discussed psychological horror games of the decade, spawned endless memes, and earned a premium console sequel. The short answer for developers is this: the 2017 original was built by Team Salvato, led by Dan Salvato, in Ren'Py , the free and open-source Ren'Py Visual Novel Engine. That niche choice did more than save money. It made the horror possible. This article explains what Ren'Py actually is, why Python fit a tiny horror experiment, and what I think the rest of us miss about transparent engines, file-system horror, and the cost of leaving niche tech.

articles.title: Zero-Downtime Kubernetes Deploys: Probes, Rolling Updates, and PodDisruptionBudgets
articles.excerpt: Kubernetes advertises rolling updates out of the box, yet many teams still see a burst of 502s on every deploy. The defaults are only part of the story: zero downtime needs correct probes, a sensible…
articles.body: Kubernetes advertises rolling updates out of the box, yet many teams still see a burst of 502s on every deploy. The defaults are only part of the story: zero downtime needs correct probes, a sensible rollout strategy, graceful shutdown, and protection from voluntary disruptions like node drains. This post walks through each piece with manifests you can apply today. Why requests get dropped During a rollout, three things can go wrong: New pods receive traffic before they are ready. The container process is running, but caches, DB pools, or JIT warm-up are not done. Old pods are killed while they still have in-flight requests. Endpoint removal and SIGTERM happen concurrently, so a pod may receive new connections after it starts shutting down. Too many pods disappear at once.

articles.title: How to Detect Look-Ahead Bias in Your Own Backtest
articles.excerpt: Look-ahead bias is the failure where your backtest uses information that did not exist yet at the moment it made a decision. You detect it mechanically, not by reading your code: compute your indicato…
articles.body: Look-ahead bias is the failure where your backtest uses information that did not exist yet at the moment it made a decision. You detect it mechanically, not by reading your code: compute your indicator twice — once over the full price history the way a vectorised backtest does, and once bar by bar on history truncated at that bar the way a live bot sees it — then compare the two values at the same bar. If they differ anywhere, something in your pipeline peeked at the future. That is the whole method, and it takes about ten lines. This matters because look-ahead is the one backtest failure that never announces itself. Overfitting at least leaves a trail: good in-sample, bad out-of-sample.

articles.title: NEAR Protocol Trading Bot: What to Test First
articles.excerpt: Before you point a trading bot at NEAR Protocol or any other coin that is trending right now, test four things first: real trading costs at today's spreads, a large enough sample of trades, how the st…
articles.body: Before you point a trading bot at NEAR Protocol or any other coin that is trending right now, test four things first: real trading costs at today's spreads, a large enough sample of trades, how the strategy did on data it never saw, and how it behaves when the hype fades. A backtest that only looks good during a hot streak usually reflects the streak, not an edge. This guide shows how to run those checks step by step. It does not say anything about where NEAR's price is going, and it won't. The goal is to judge the bot, not the coin. Why trending coins are a trap for backtests When a coin like NEAR Protocol, Injective or Optimism shows up on trending lists, three things usually change at once: Volatility jumps. Bigger candles mean bigger wins and bigger losses per trade.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 13, 1773: Astronomer Charles Messier discovers the Whirlpool Galaxy before we ever knew it was a galaxy
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 13, 1773, a French astronomer named Charles Messier discovered the "Whirlpool Galaxy," also known as Messier 51, or M51. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 13, 1773, a French astronomer named Charles Messier discovered the " Whirlpool Galaxy , " also known as Messier 51, or M51. Charles Messier was scanning the sky for objects that could confuse comet hunters when he catalogued the galaxy as M51. However, Messier wasn't able to see the spiral structure, and he didn't identify it as a galaxy. Seventy-two years later, another astronomer named William Parsons saw the whirlpool shape, but he thought it was a spiral nebula. Eventually, Edwin Hubble found out that M51 and other features like it were actually galaxies. Spiral galaxy M51 (NGC 5194), The Whirlpool Galaxy, displays its long arms which consist of stars and gas laced with dust arranged in long lanes, in this view from the Hubble Space Telescope.

articles.body: NEW YORK — Set your phasers to back-to-school, space fans. Star Trek is going back to Starfleet Academy for season 2, and we finally have a release date. The sophomore season of " Star Trek: Starfleet Academy " will warp back to the small screen in March 2027 when the limited series returns for its final season on Paramount+ . The series, which follows a class of cadets balancing Starfleet classes, space adventures (and yes, some love) in the 32nd century, will return with its full cast and even add new faces, showrunners announced at a panel at New York Comic Con 2026 on Saturday (Oct. 10). "Season one is about letting go of who you were in the past to start again at Starfleet Academy," executive producer and co-showrunner Noga Landau said in the Star Trek panel.

articles.title: See the original Galileo shuttle from 'Star Trek' in its new home at the Original Series Set Tour in New York
articles.excerpt: This iconic spaceship will now live long and prosper in its brand-new Star Trek Tour home.
articles.body: Nostalgia is a hell of a thing, especially when it comes to sci-fi. For "Star Trek" fans wanting to mark the franchise's 60th anniversary this year, a geeky pilgrimage to upstate New York should be on the cards. Why? Because alongside the splendid autumnal colors, they can steer over to Ticonderoga to behold the newly installed Galileo shuttlecraft. After a complete two-year restoration project in 2012 headed up by superfan and collector Adam Schneider, this iconic fictional spacecraft, seen by millions in seven episodes over three seasons of "Star Trek: The Original Series," was recently relocated from its former home at the Johnson Space Center Museum in Houston, Texas.

articles.title: Earth's poles shifted surprisingly fast during the age of dinosaurs, ancient sea levels reveal
articles.excerpt: The location of Earth's geographic poles has changed several times over the past 320 million years in a process known as true polar wander.
articles.body: The location of Earth's geographic poles has changed several times over the past 320 million years in a process known as true polar wander, according to measurements of ancient flooding brought about by sea level changes resulting from our planet's crust shifting relative to Earth's spin axis. Such a shift can affect climate, both on local scales and globally, as regions that were by the poles find themselves moving down to lower latitudes and vice versa. This can then affect atmospheric circulation patterns, which affect climate across the world. The changes would have affected the environments in which life developed and evolved, from the age of the dinosaurs through to some of our oldest primate ancestors.
